transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Hi, thank you so much for seeing me. I hope I'm in the right place. Um... is it okay if I just explain what's been happening at work? 

I do bookkeeping, and I've always tried to be really thorough, which is a good thing, right? But lately... I guess I've been having a hard time stopping. I keep going back over the exact same spreadsheets and calculations again and again. I'll end up staying at the office for hours after everyone else leaves, even when I know I've already checked everything. 

It's just... I get this really bad feeling that if I don't do it just one more time, something awful is going to happen and it'll be entirely my fault. I'm sorry, I know it probably sounds a bit silly to be so hung up on math... does that make sense?
Do you find that these worries or thoughts feel intrusive and unwanted, and do you feel that you have to do these checks to prevent something bad from happening?

Yes, exactly. I hope I'm explaining this right, but yes, they definitely feel unwanted. It's actually a little embarrassing to talk about, because I really don't want you to think I'm incompetent or bad at my job. I'm actually a very good employee! 

But... even after I know the numbers match, this thought just keeps jumping in. It tells me that I missed one hidden mistake in the payroll or the taxes, and that somebody's check won't go through, or the firm will get in huge trouble. I try so hard to just push it away and move on, but it comes right back. It's honestly like I can't even trust my own eyes anymore. So I feel like I have to do the checks just to make sure I don't ruin anything for anyone else. 

Am I making sense? I really hope that answers your question.
